claims.explanation: SB-590885 is a selective BRAF inhibitor that kills cancer lines dependent on oncogenic BRAF-driven MAPK signaling, so sensitivity is best explained by activating BRAF mutations (especially V600E) and by a BRAF-mutant/oncogene-addicted transcriptional context. Lines without BRAF mutations, or with alternative RAS/MAPK activation such as KRAS or NRAS mutations, are generally less affected because they do not depend on the drug's target. Co-occurring PTEN/PI3K pathway alterations may further modulate sensitivity through downstream survival signaling.

features.basis: Oncogenic BRAF alleles confer selective sensitivity to SB-590885 (PMID 17145850); most killed lines carry BRAF mutations.
KRAS-mutant lines are enriched among least-affected lines, consistent with RAS-driven MAPK activation bypassing BRAF dependence.
NRAS-mutant melanoma lines (IPC298) are less sensitive, consistent with RAF-independent MAPK activation.
PTEN loss/PI3K activation may cooperate with BRAF inhibition; PTEN-mutant lines appear among sensitive lines.
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK upstream of RAF, potentially reducing dependence on BRAF; NF1-mutant lines appear in both groups but several are least affected.
MEK1 mutation (NCIH1437) can activate ERK downstream of RAF, bypassing BRAF inhibition.
EGFR-mutant lung lines (HCC4006, NCIH1650) are least affected, consistent with EGFR-driven MAPK signaling independent of BRAF.
Higher BRAF expression may increase dependence on BRAF signaling; virtual cell shows MAPK pathway transcriptional responses in BRAF-mutant lines.
DUSP6 is a MAPK feedback target downregulated by SB-590885 in HT29, indicating active MAPK pathway dependence.
MYC downregulation in the virtual cell response suggests MAPK-driven proliferation is targeted in sensitive lines.
PIK3CA-mutant lines appear among least affected, suggesting PI3K activation can compensate for MAPK inhibition.
IGF-1R/PI3K signaling mediates resistance to BRAF inhibitors including SB-590885.
